thesis: MP Materials owns and operates Mountain Pass, the only integrated rare earth mine and processing site in the Western Hemisphere, and is building a domestic magnet supply chain aimed squarely at the U.S. effort to break China's rare earth dominance. A July 2025 Department of Defense public-private partnership made the Pentagon the largest shareholder and set a $110/kg NdPr price floor plus a 10-year magnet offtake and EBITDA guarantee, while a $500M Apple agreement anchors commercial demand for recycled magnets. The catch: MP is still deeply unprofitable (FY2025 net loss $85.9M, free cash flow -$328M) and the equity is priced on a magnet ramp that does not commission until 2028, so this is a high-conviction thesis with binary execution risk — a SPEC. BUY into a 52-week-low pullback near $41.

drivers: 10X magnet campus in Northlake, Texas commissions on schedule and ramps toward the 10,000 metric ton nameplate, turning MP into a Western magnet supplier at scale
NdPr prices recover well above the $110/kg DoD floor as ex-China demand from EVs, robotics, defense and AI hardware tightens
DoD offtake, $140M minimum EBITDA guarantee and the $500M Apple agreement de-risk demand and pull profitability forward
Government policy tailwinds (tariffs, export controls, reshoring incentives) reward the only U.S. integrated producer
Analyst high targets prove right — Canaccord $82, Needham $73, Morgan Stanley $71.50 — with consensus average near $79–80

base_case.assumptions: Rare earth concentrate and NdPr volumes keep growing at a ~40-50% revenue clip off a small base; the DoD price floor and Apple/offtake contracts stabilize demand; 10X construction stays broadly on track for 2028 commissioning; losses narrow but the company stays FCF-negative through the build-out, funded by its ~$1.8B cash pile; the stock re-rates back toward its 50-/200-day moving averages ($56–59) as sentiment stabilizes.

risks: 10X magnet facility slips, runs over its >$1.25B budget, or ramps slowly — pushing the profitability inflection past 2028
NdPr prices stay weak and China floods supply, leaving MP reliant on the DoD floor and eroding the growth narrative
Continued heavy cash burn (FY2025 FCF -$328M) forces dilutive equity or debt raises
The rich valuation (forward P/E ~150x, P/S ~21x) compresses as growth stocks de-rate, driving further downgrades
Single-site concentration risk at Mountain Pass — any operational or geological setback hits the whole thesis

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — NdPr oxide production/sales, Magnetics segment revenue, cash burn and updated 10X timeline
10X magnet campus (Northlake, TX) construction and equipment-procurement milestones ahead of 2028 commissioning
10X facility commissioning — first large-scale U.S. rare earth magnet output
NdPr price relative to the $110/kg DoD floor and ramp of the 10-year DoD magnet offtake
Apple $500M recycled-magnet deliveries and additional commercial magnet offtake wins

key_risks: Deep unprofitability and cash burn — FY2025 net loss $85.9M, operating margin -89%, free cash flow -$328M; profitability hinges on a magnet ramp that does not commission until 2028
Extreme valuation — forward P/E ~150x and P/S ~21x price in years of execution; any stumble drives sharp de-rating
Execution risk on the >$1.25B 10X magnet campus — budget, schedule and ramp all unproven
Rare earth price volatility and China's dominance of global supply, pricing and processing
Single-site concentration at Mountain Pass — operational, geological or permitting setbacks hit the entire business
Policy dependence — the thesis leans heavily on continued DoD support, tariffs and reshoring incentives
Dilution risk from the DoD convertible preferred and future capital raises to fund the build-out
